subject: Pilot timebox addendum: compression discount mechanics and invoice flow
messages:
From: Eleni Petros <eleni@fathom.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, procurement@fathom.ai
Cc: cloudops@fathom.ai
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot update + ask on discount mechanics

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the check-in last week. We wrapped a fresh usage snapshot (attached) from the past two weeks of the pilot and have a couple of asks before we sign the addendum:

1) Can you explain how the "compression discount" would be calculated in practice? Our infra team noted that most of our calls already use payload compression and significant batching — we want to understand whether this is a usage-based rebate, a one-time credit, or a per-invoice line item.

2) If we go with the 3-week timebox extension you mentioned, what will the invoice flow look like? We need clarity for our procurement team: will the extender show as a separate invoice, a credit on the next invoice, or a pro-rata top-up?

3) Any chance we can include a short SLA for latency degradation during the extended window? We had two spikes last Tuesday and our product team is nervous about ramping to production.

We're copying procurement and cloudops so they can flag any compliance/billing needs. 

Attachment: POC_usage_report_2026-08-09.pdf

Best,
Eleni
Head of Product
Fathom Analytics

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Eleni Petros <eleni@fathom.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, procurement@fathom.ai, cloudops@fathom.ai
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot update + ask on discount mechanics

Hi Eleni — thanks for the report and the clear questions. Quick answers below, and attached is a draft addendum for the 3-week timebox we discussed.

- Compression discount mechanics: it's a usage-driven discount applied at invoice time. We measure the effective billed tokens after our token-normalization and compression heuristics. If your average effective tokens/request for the billing period stays below the agreed threshold (we can propose 40% lower than baseline usage) you get a graduated rebate of 5–15% on generation tokens for that invoice. It's not a one-off credit — it's applied to the invoice where the condition is satisfied.

- Invoice flow options (we can pick one):
  1) Separate addendum invoice for the extension (payable on signature) and then monthly invoicing resumes — easiest for procurement.
  2) Post-period rebate credit applied on the next monthly invoice showing both the gross charge and the rebate line.
  3) Pro-rata top-up billed immediately for the extension days (if you want cashflow neutrality).

- SLA: For the extension window we can commit to a 99.5% availability target at the route level and offer a one-time service credit (capped) if we miss it due to infra issues. That will need approval from Ops/Infra but is doable for a short pilot addendum.

I've flagged this to Grace (CS) for the SLA details and David (Finance/Legal) for the billing wording. Attached: redwood_pilot_addendum_v1.pdf and pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx (shows thresholds and the rebate ladder).

If you prefer, we can turn the rebate into a single invoice credit instead of a recurring invoice-line rebate — that is usually simpler for procurement but is less tightly coupled to the actual run-rate. Let me know what procurement prefers and we'll update the DocuSign.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Eleni Petros <eleni@fathom.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@fathom.ai, cloudops@fathom.ai
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot update + ask on discount mechanics

Jordan — thanks for the clarity. A couple of follow-ups:

- Procurement preference is option (2) — post-period rebate as a line item on the next invoice. They want the rebate language explicit for bookkeeping.

- For the SLA, we need the definition of "route-level availability" in writing and an outline of the remediation credit calculation (we can share our internal template).

- Is the rebate tied to a metrics signal we can both observe? Ideally we'd have a shared dashboard or a snapshot export so our ops team can validate the threshold without back-and-forth.

Can Grace loop in a short technical contact (from your infra/Optimize team) and can David confirm whether the rebate can be represented as a single-line credit if necessary for accounting? Once we have those items, we can route the addendum through DocuSign.

Thanks,
Eleni

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Eleni Petros <eleni@fathom.ai>, procurement@fathom.ai
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot update + ask on discount mechanics

Eleni / team —

Quick internal note and next steps (forwarding to you for transparency):

- Grace: I've asked Sara (Optimize eng) to stand up a shared chart that shows effective billed tokens per day and the compression ratio. She'll have a one-off export we can link to the HubSpot deal and we can grant view access.

- David: procurement prefers post-period rebate (invoice line). Can Finance confirm if we can represent that as a contra-revenue line (single-line credit) for accounting purposes? If not, we fall back to a separate credit note.

- Legal/ops: I'll mark the SLA as "pilot addendum SLA" in the DocuSign draft and include the remediation credit table (capped at one invoice's value for the extension period).

I'll update the addendum to reflect procurement's preference and push a DocuSign link to this thread once Grace confirms the dashboard link. Proposed sign-by date: 2026-08-18 to keep the pilot continuous.

Attachments: pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx (internal)

Jordan
